prompt: What does an energy above the convex hull (E_hull) equal to 0 eV/atom indicate in a materials database?

options.text: The phase is predicted to be thermodynamically stable against competing phases in that database at 0 K
options.why: On-hull phases have E_hull = 0 relative to the competing entries in the same functional set.

options.text: The material has a zero band gap and must be a metal
options.why: E_hull measures thermodynamic stability, not electronic band gap.

options.text: The calculation failed to converge
options.why: E_hull = 0 means the entry sits on the lower convex hull.

hints: Distinguish thermodynamic phase stability from electronic band structure.

prompt: Why should you treat band gaps listed in a high-throughput GGA/GGA+U database with caution?

options.text: Semi-local GGA functionals systematically underestimate semiconductor and insulator band gaps
options.why: Derivative discontinuity errors in semi-local DFT lead to underestimated gaps.

options.text: Databases only store optical absorption coefficients, not band gaps
options.why: Materials Project stores Kohn-Sham band gaps, which reflect the chosen functional.

options.text: GGA always overestimates band gaps by a factor of three
options.why: Semi-local GGA underestimates rather than overestimates band gaps.

hints: Recall the functional ladder and band-gap problem from Module 5.

prompt: Why does Materials Screening display a prominent synthetic-data banner when running on sample fixtures?

options.text: So demonstration rows are never mistaken for real Materials Project entries before an author data pull
options.why: Honest provenance prevents users from citing synthetic test rows as real materials data.

options.text: Because browser JavaScript cannot read real JSON files
options.why: The same query engine reads both the sample fixture and the real snapshot.

options.text: Because CSV export only works on synthetic data
options.why: CSV export works on any loaded snapshot.

prompt: Why is filtering by site count (nsites) useful before launching a first VASP project from a screening shortlist?

options.text: Plane-wave DFT scales steeply with atom count and volume, so smaller cells give faster starter runs
options.why: Keeping starter cells compact makes convergence testing and debugging practical.

options.text: VASP rejects any POSCAR with more than 10 atoms
options.why: VASP supports large supercells, but compute cost grows rapidly with atom count.

options.text: Larger cells never require k-points
options.why: k-mesh density depends on reciprocal lattice lengths, not just atom count.

hints: Think about computational scaling with electron count.

prompt: What does the live validity panel in the Material Builder check before you export a POSCAR?

options.text: Geometric and chemical issues such as overlapping atoms, collapsed cells, or thin vacuum
options.why: Catching severe overlaps and cell issues locally prevents immediate VASP failures.

options.text: Whether your HPC cluster queue is currently empty
options.why: The Material Builder runs offline in the browser with no cluster connection.

options.text: The exact experimental melting point of the crystal
options.why: Validity rules check structure geometry and chemistry, not melting points.

hints: Recall rules B001 through B012 in the Material Builder.

prompt: Which ISIF setting should you use in VASP when relaxing a slab or a molecule placed in a vacuum box?

options.text: ISIF = 2 (relax atomic positions while keeping cell shape and volume fixed)
options.why: ISIF = 3 would collapse the vacuum gap.

options.text: ISIF = 3 (relax cell volume and shape freely)
options.why: ISIF = 3 shrinks the vacuum region around a slab or molecule.

options.text: ISIF = 7 (change volume only)
options.why: Volume relaxation collapses the vacuum gap.

hints: Think about what happens to empty vacuum space if VASP optimizes the cell volume.

prompt: How does the Material Builder detect severely overlapping atoms in a periodic crystal?

options.text: By comparing periodic minimum-image pair distances against Cordero covalent radii
options.why: Periodic minimum-image checks catch overlaps both inside the cell and across cell boundaries.

options.text: By running a full VASP SCF calculation in the browser
options.why: The overlap check is a fast geometric distance check.

options.text: By checking only the file size in bytes
options.why: File size says nothing about interatomic distances.

prompt: What is the purpose of Molecule mode's 'Clean up in 3D' button?

options.text: It generates a rough starting 3D geometry for DFT using a valence-geometry heuristic, not a final quantum-chemical optimization
options.why: The 3D clean-up gives a reasonable starting POSCAR/XYZ that still needs DFT relaxation.

options.text: It runs CCSD(T) in the browser to compute exact bond lengths
options.why: It uses a lightweight local valence-geometry heuristic labelled with a Heuristic badge.

options.text: It deletes all hydrogen atoms before export
options.why: It expands explicit hydrogens so every atom has 3D coordinates.
